pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 📝 **Strand 2 — Productivity Software**
Sub-strand 3: Introduction to Electronic Spreadsheet

Shopkeepers, teachers, nurses, farmers and bankers all keep records and do calculations. An electronic spreadsheet lets them do this quickly and accurately. In this unit you will explore Microsoft Excel, enter and format data, prepare worksheets for printing, use AutoFill and write your first formulas.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B7.2.3.1** Demonstrate how to use the spreadsheet (Editing Worksheets).
- **B7.2.3.2** Demonstrate how to format a worksheet.
- **B7.2.3.3** Demonstrate how to use spreadsheet formulas.

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B7.2.3.1.1** Explain the importance of electronic spreadsheets.
- **B7.2.3.1.2** Explore features of the MS-Excel interface.
- **B7.2.3.1.3** Demonstrate how to set the cell data type (General, Number, Currency, etc.).
- **B7.2.3.1.4** Demonstrate how to use Align Text, Merge & Wrap, Borders and Shades.
- **B7.2.3.2.1** Demonstrate how to adjust margins and set page orientation.
- **B7.2.3.2.2** Demonstrate how to set up a header and a footer.
- **B7.2.3.2.3** Demonstrate the use of the AutoFill function.
- **B7.2.3.3.1** Demonstrate how to create formulas.

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 6.1 The Importance of Electronic Spreadsheets
- 6.2 Exploring the Excel Interface
- 6.3 Setting Cell Data Types (Number Formats)
- 6.4 Alignment, Merge & Wrap, Borders and Shading
- 6.5 Page Margins, Orientation and Worksheet Views
- 6.6 Headers and Footers
- 6.7 Using AutoFill
- 6.8 Creating Simple Formulas

**Core competencies developed:** Digital Literacy (DL5.1), Creativity and Innovation (CI5.4), Critical Thinking and Problem Solving (CP5.1).

pages.title: The Importance of Electronic Spreadsheets
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.3.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explain the meaning of an electronic spreadsheet;
- state its benefits;
- name common spreadsheet packages.
A **spreadsheet** is a grid of **rows** and **columns** used to organise, calculate and analyse numerical data. An **electronic spreadsheet** is software that does this on a computer. When a number changes, every calculation that depends on it is **updated automatically**.
## Benefits of electronic spreadsheets
- Fast and accurate **calculations** with formulas and functions.
- **Automatic recalculation** when data changes.
- Easy to **sort, filter and search** large amounts of data.
- Data can be turned into **charts and graphs** in seconds.
- Useful for **budgets, school records, payroll, stock records, timetables and scientific data**.
- Worksheets can be saved, printed, shared and reused as templates.
| **Software** | **Notes** |
|---|---|
| Microsoft Excel | Part of Microsoft 365; files saved as .xlsx |
| Google Sheets | Free, browser-based, collaborative |
| LibreOffice Calc | Free and open-source |
| Apple Numbers | Free on Apple devices |
| Lotus 1-2-3 | Very popular in the 1980s–90s; discontinued in 2014 |
| VisiCalc | The first electronic spreadsheet (1979) |

pages.title: Exploring the Excel Interface
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.3.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- identify the parts of the Excel window;
- insert, select, delete and move data.
[[fig:c7-f15|Figure 14: The Microsoft Excel window]]
| **Term** | **Meaning** |
|---|---|
| Workbook | An Excel file; it contains one or more worksheets |
| Worksheet (sheet) | One grid of cells; shown by a sheet tab at the bottom |
| Column | A vertical line of cells labelled with letters (A, B, C … XFD: 16,384 columns) |
| Row | A horizontal line of cells labelled with numbers (1 to 1,048,576) |
| Cell | The box where a column and a row meet |
| Cell address (reference) | The column letter followed by the row number, e.g. **C4** |
| Active cell | The selected cell, with a thick border; its address appears in the Name Box |
| Range | A rectangular group of cells written with a colon, e.g. **A1:C5** |
| Name Box | Shows the address of the active cell |
| Formula bar | Shows and edits the contents or formula of the active cell |

pages.title: Working with data
pages.body:
## Working with data
| **Task** | **How to do it** |
|---|---|
| Enter data | Click a cell, type, then press **Enter** (moves down) or **Tab** (moves right) |
| Edit a cell | Double-click the cell or press **F2**, or edit in the formula bar |
| Select a range | Drag across the cells; click a column letter or row number to select it all; **Ctrl + A** selects the sheet |
| Delete data | Select the cells and press **Delete** (clears contents only) |
| Insert a row or column | Right-click a row number or column letter › **Insert** (or Home › Cells › Insert) |
| Delete a row or column | Right-click the row number or column letter › **Delete** |
| Move data | Select the cells, point to the border until the pointer becomes a four-headed arrow, then drag; or **Ctrl + X**, **Ctrl + V** |
| Widen a column | Drag the boundary to the right of the column letter, or double-click it to AutoFit |
> 💻 **Practical session — Sample data set**
Enter this data starting in cell A1. Then insert a new row above row 3 and add **Kofi, 62, 70**. Delete the Science score for Efua and move the whole table so it starts at cell B2.
| **Name** | **Maths** | **Science** |
|---|---|---|
| Abena | 78 | 85 |
| Efua | 91 | 88 |
| Kwesi | 55 | 67 |
| Mariam | 84 | 90 |

pages.title: Setting Cell Data Types (Number Formats)
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.3.1.3
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- enter values, text, dates and times;
- set and modify the number format of cells.
Excel recognises different kinds of data: **text (labels)**, **numbers (values)**, **dates**, **times** and **formulas**. Text aligns to the left by default; numbers, dates and times align to the right. A **number format** changes how a value is displayed without changing the value itself.
| **Format** | **Example display** | **Use** |
|---|---|---|
| General | 1234.5 | Default; no special format |
| Number | 1,234.50 | Choose decimal places and thousand separator |
| Currency | GH₵1,234.50 | Money; symbol next to the number |
| Accounting | GH₵ 1,234.50 | Money; symbols and decimals line up in a column; zero shows as a dash |
| Short Date / Long Date | 17/11/2026 or 17 November 2026 | Dates |
| Time | 14:30:00 or 2:30 PM | Times |
| Percentage | 85% | Values multiplied by 100 with a % sign |
| Fraction | 1/2 | Displays decimals as fractions |
| Scientific | 1.23E+03 | Very large or very small numbers |
| Text | 0244123456 | Treats the entry as text (keeps the leading zero of phone numbers) |
> 🪜 **Step by step — Changing a number format**
1. Select the cells to format.
2. Click **Home › Number** and choose a format from the drop-down list, or use the **Accounting**, **Percent** and **Comma** buttons; use **Increase/Decrease Decimal** to adjust decimal places.
3. For more options, press **Ctrl + 1** to open **Format Cells › Number**. For the cedi, choose **Currency**, open the **Symbol** list and select **GH₵** (English, Ghana).

pages.title: Setting Cell Data Types (Number Formats) (continued)
pages.body:
> 💻 **Practical session**
In a new sheet, type the price of five school items in column B and format them as **Currency (GH₵)** with two decimal places. In column C enter purchase dates and format them as **Long Date**. In column D enter times of purchase and format them as **Time**.

pages.title: Alignment, Merge & Wrap, Borders and Shading
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.3.1.4
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- change horizontal and vertical alignment;
- merge cells and wrap text;
- apply borders and shading to a worksheet.
| **Command (Home › Alignment)** | **What it does** |
|---|---|
| Top / Middle / Bottom Align | Vertical alignment of contents within the cell |
| Align Left / Centre / Align Right | Horizontal alignment |
| Orientation | Rotates text, e.g. angle counter-clockwise or vertical |
| Wrap Text | Displays long text on several lines within one cell |
| Merge & Centre | Joins selected cells into one and centres the contents (great for titles) |
| Merge Across / Merge Cells / Unmerge Cells | Other merge options from the drop-down arrow |
| Increase / Decrease Indent | Moves the contents away from or towards the cell edge |
> 🪜 **Step by step — Adding borders and shading (group work)**
1. Select the table range, e.g. A1:D6.
2. Click the arrow beside **Home › Font › Borders** and choose **All Borders**. Choose **Thick Outside Borders** for a strong outline.
3. Select the heading row and click **Fill Colour** (paint bucket) to shade it; change its **Font Colour** to white for contrast.
4. For more styles, press **Ctrl + 1 › Border** and **Fill** tabs.
> 💻 **Practical session — Format a class record sheet**
Type the title **B7 GOLD – FIRST TERM RESULTS** in A1 and merge and centre it across A1:E1. Wrap the text in the heading “Continuous Assessment Score”. Centre all scores horizontally and vertically, add all borders, and shade the heading row.

pages.title: Page Margins, Orientation and Worksheet Views
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.3.2.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- adjust margins and set page orientation for printing;
- adjust margins on different page sizes;
- display a worksheet in different views.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Preparing a worksheet for printing**
1. Click the **Page Layout** tab.
2. Click **Margins** and choose **Normal**, **Wide** or **Narrow**, or **Custom Margins** to type exact values (e.g. top 2 cm).
3. Click **Orientation** and choose **Portrait** (tall) or **Landscape** (wide, good for many columns).
4. Click **Size** and choose the paper size (**A4** is standard in Ghana; also Letter, Legal, A3).
5. Click **File › Print** (**Ctrl + P**) to check the print preview before printing.
## Worksheet views (View › Workbook Views)
| **View** | **Description** |
|---|---|
| Normal | The default view for entering data |
| Page Layout | Shows pages as they will print, with margins, headers and footers; you can edit headers here |
| Page Break Preview | Shows blue lines where pages break; drag them to adjust |
| Custom Views | Saves display and print settings to use again |
> 🧪 **Activity**
Change the page size of your results sheet to A4, then to A3, and observe how the margins and page breaks change in **Page Layout** and **Page Break Preview** views.

pages.title: Headers and Footers
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.3.2.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- set up header and footer elements;
- insert page numbers, current date, time and file name.
A **header** appears at the top of every printed page and a **footer** at the bottom. They are used for titles, school names, page numbers, dates and file names.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Inserting a header and footer**
1. Click **Insert › Text › Header & Footer**. Excel switches to **Page Layout** view and the cursor is in the centre header section.
2. Type the header text, e.g. ST. PETER’S JHS – B7 RESULTS. The left and right sections can hold other text.
3. Click **Go to Footer** on the **Header & Footer** tab. In the footer, use the **Header & Footer Elements** buttons: **Page Number**, **Number of Pages**, **Current Date**, **Current Time**, **File Path**, **File Name**, **Sheet Name**, **Picture**.
4. Click any cell on the sheet to finish, then return to **View › Normal**.
> ✨ **Did you know?** Excel shows elements as codes, for example &[Page] of &[Pages], &[Date], &[Time] and &[File]. They update automatically when you print.

pages.title: Using AutoFill
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.3.2.3
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- use the fill handle to generate series of days, months and numbers;
- create multiplication tables with AutoFill.
The **fill handle** is the small square at the bottom-right corner of the active cell or selection. Dragging it **copies** data or **continues a series** automatically. This is called **AutoFill**.
| **Type in the first cell(s)** | **Drag the fill handle down** | **Result** |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | to 7 cells | Monday, Tuesday … Sunday |
| Jan | to 12 cells | Jan, Feb … Dec |
| January | to 12 cells | January … December |
| 1 and 2 (select both) | to 10 cells | 1, 2, 3 … 10 (counting numbers) |
| 1 and 3 (select both) | to 10 cells | 1, 3, 5 … 19 (odd numbers) |
| 2 and 4 | to 10 cells | 2, 4, 6 … 20 (even numbers) |
| Term 1 | to 3 cells | Term 1, Term 2, Term 3 |
> ✏️ **Worked example — Building the 7 times table with AutoFill**
1. In A1 type 1 and in A2 type 2. Select both and drag the fill handle down to A12 to get 1 to 12.
2. In B1 type 7.
3. In C1 type the formula =A1∗$B$1 and press Enter (the $ signs keep B1 fixed; you will study this in Basic 8).
4. Drag the fill handle of C1 down to C12. Column C now shows 7, 14, 21 … 84.
5. Change B1 to 9 and the whole table changes to the 9 times table instantly.

pages.title: Using AutoFill (continued)
pages.body: You can also use **Home › Editing › Fill › Series** to set a step value (e.g. 5, 10, 15 …) and a stop value.

pages.title: Creating Simple Formulas
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.3.3.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- create formulas starting with the equals sign;
- use arithmetic operators and cell references;
- apply the order of operations.
A **formula** is an instruction that performs a calculation. In Excel, **every formula starts with an equals sign (=)**. Formulas should use **cell references** (like B2) rather than typed numbers, so that the answer updates when the data changes.
| **Operator** | **Meaning** | **Example formula** | **Result if A1 = 12, B1 = 4** |
|---|---|---|---|
| + | Addition | =A1+B1 | 16 |
| - | Subtraction | =A1-B1 | 8 |
| ∗ | Multiplication | =A1∗B1 | 48 |
| / | Division | =A1/B1 | 3 |
| ^ | Exponent (power) | =B1^2 | 16 |
| % | Percentage | =A1∗25% | 3 |
> 🎯 **BECE focus — Order of operations** Excel follows **BODMAS**: Brackets first, then Orders (powers), then Division and Multiplication (left to right), then Addition and Subtraction (left to right). =2+3∗4 gives **14**, but =(2+3)∗4 gives **20**.
> ✏️ **Worked example — A shopping bill**
|  | **A** | **B** | **C** | **D** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Item | Unit price (GH₵) | Quantity | Cost |
| 2 | Exercise book | 5.00 | 6 | =B2∗C2 → 30.00 |
| 3 | Pen | 2.50 | 4 | =B3∗C3 → 10.00 |
| 4 | Mathematical set | 25.00 | 1 | =B4∗C4 → 25.00 |
| 5 |  |  | TOTAL | =D2+D3+D4 → 65.00 |
Type each formula in column D, then press Enter. If the price of a pen changes to 3.00, the cost and the total update automatically.

pages.title: Creating Simple Formulas (continued)
pages.body:
> 💻 **Practical session — Your first spreadsheet project**
Create a sheet showing the scores of five learners in **Class Test (out of 20)**, **Exercises (out of 20)** and **Exam (out of 60)**. Use formulas to calculate each learner’s **Total** (out of 100) and **Percentage of the class test** (=B2/20∗100). Format the sheet with a merged title, borders, shading, a header with the school name and a footer with the page number and date.

pages.title: Review: written and practical tasks
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. State **four** uses of a spreadsheet in a school.
2. Explain the difference between the Currency and Accounting formats.
3. Describe how to set a worksheet to landscape orientation with narrow margins.
4. Explain how AutoFill can be used to produce odd numbers from 1 to 49.
5. Write formulas to (a) add A2 and B2, (b) find the average of C1, C2 and C3, (c) find 15% of D4.
